anti_generic_signature_read: Round 2, unprimed, naming the least generic thing before knowing what it was: 'The spur ring. Seen in rim-detail.png these are not the blunt triangles of a gear: each is a slender gold blade with a wide swept flange on one side tapering to a fine hooked tip, and they all sweep the same direction around the circle, giving the whole disc a consistent rotational lean. Combined with the arcaded skirt underneath it is the one part of this object with real character.'
blind_action_read: Round 2, unprimed, on the old sheet: 'Nothing moves ... two identical frames and one pop-in' - a rendering artifact, not a depicted change. The sheet was rebuilt as three exact states at one fixed top camera. Round 3 fresh observation (primed, disclosed): 'One brown counter now sits on the hub ... The lone brown counter at the bottom, at roughly 5 o'clock, is gone ... The lane that held the solitary brown is now occupied by a cream counter ... Nothing else changed ... The three changes are one event: a cream counter travelled from 1:30 down to the lane at 5 o'clock that held a single brown; the brown it landed on was lifted off the board and placed on the hub.'
blind_form_read: Round 2, unprimed: 'Still emphatically 2.5D ... a wafer whose height is maybe 6-7% of its diameter, sitting on a short skirt of pointed feet. The plan outline in top.png is now a genuinely clean circle - the wedge tips terminate at a consistent radius and the lumpy, bitten silhouette I would expect from a rough boolean is not there. The wedges themselves are dead-flat horizontal plates ... The hub is a flat tan pancake with a small chamfer at its top edge. Surfaces read as raw flat-shaded CAD: crisp arrises everywhere ... The perimeter spurs are the only genuinely three-dimensional event.'
blind_held_read: Round 2, unprimed: 'A thin, flat sunburst disc - a striped circular platter or medallion with a raised plain hub, a scatter of small brown and cream lumps on its face, and a ring of slender swept spurs around its edge ... a decorative trivet, coaster or spinner base.' It named a sun-shaped disc but not a game, which was treated as a fault in the evidence: the signature sheet was then three near-identical panels. After the sheet was rebuilt to show the hit, the same critic - disclosed as primed - read 'A round, sun-shaped backgammon board - twenty-four radial lanes in four banks of six around a central bar', and drew the line itself: 'the images alone carry the game ... a viewer who knows backgammon would name it from this sheet without being told', but 'the images alone do not carry coronal rain'. No naive recognition of the coronal-rain subject is claimed.
blind_relationship_read: Round 2, unprimed: 'The hub sits on top of and centered over the wedge field, covering the inner ends of every wedge. The wedges radiate out from beneath it, stacked on a gold base plate. The base plate's edge carries the spur ring, which surrounds everything and also drops below the disc as a skirt, so the spurs both flank and underhang the whole assembly. The small lumps sit on top of the wedges in short arcs and marching lines running roughly radially outward.'
blind_subjects_read: Round 2, unprimed: 'Four kinds. (1) Radial wedges, roughly 26-28, alternating canary yellow and khaki-tan. (2) Perimeter spurs, roughly 28-30, gold, slender and hooked. (3) One central hub disc, about a third of overall diameter. (4) Small applied lumps, roughly 28-32 total: about 16 dark chocolate-brown, about 14 off-white/cream.' The counts are its estimates off an orthographic render; the exact plan measures 24 tiles, 38 tongues, one centre bar and 30 counters, and it withdrew its tongue count in round 3.

largest_risk: Two disclosed risks, both required by the Wish and both reported. (1) The outermost counter: 0.90769 of its footprint lands on its own tile and the rest passes the 89.85 mm tile arc. The Wish requires that figure to stay at or above 0.90769, so it sits exactly at its floor with no margin; adjacent-tile contact is 0.0 mm2. (2) The underside arcade: seen from below or at a very low angle the webs between tongue roots still carry a fluted, crimped quality - the one place the critic's bottle-cap association survives. Trough floors and depths are preserved geometry the Wish forbids changing, and it also forbids removing underside material, so that arcade cannot be altered without breaking the brief. Above the parting line, the view the board is used in, the critic's ranking is unambiguous: blades of flame first, gear teeth 'wrong'. Separately, print readiness is not claimed: wall and overhang passed on all 55 parts at 0.4 mm, but the verifier's print-gate tier was not opened, so print_gate_sha256s is empty and the product seals as a disclosed prototype.
resolution: Passed at round 3 with no blocking visual defect. Round 1 was a naive blind read of the first build; the critic ranked the rim 'a crimped, bottle-cap-meets-gear-tooth crown' - the exact fault this correction removes - so the rim was repaired inside the three levers the Wish allows: curl raised to 37.41-43.22 deg with 29.91-34.56 inside the outer half, the early taper deepened until mid length is 0.268 of the root, and the fall moved to start at the root chord so the ramp runs the blade's whole length, with a rim collar fused back under the tile lips. Round 2 was a fresh unprimed read of the repaired images followed by the reveal: the critic then ranked 'blades of flame laid back off a disc' first, said 'gear teeth is wrong', matched every positive requirement and found every negative absent. Its remaining doubts rested on a weak signature sheet and three misreads, so the sheet was rebuilt as three exact states showing the hit. Round 3 is disclosed as primed and no naive recognition is claimed for it; on the measurements it withdrew the tile-overlap and tongue-count items and reclassified the counter overhang and underside arcade as disclosed risks required by the brief. Its verdict: 'None remains. I can find no visible departure from any of P1-P8 or N1-N7 in these images.'
reviewer: One independent native critic (subagent a54eff289d32695c8) given only the canonical images and told to read no other file. Three rounds; round 3 disclosed as primed.
